transcript.speaker: Samuel Anderson
transcript.content: Hey Ethan — can we talk for a minute about our passing? I’ve noticed some awkward or soft passes that make it hard to run plays, and I think a few focused drills could tighten our timing. Could we try a short routine next practice — 10 minutes of target passing, a serve‑receive pattern, and a 3-person continuous drill — and agree on simple cues like calling “mine” or “set”? I can lead it if you’re down; what do you think or is there a drill you’d rather try?

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Hey Sam — I hear you and I’m glad you brought it up. I tend to favor softer, placement-focused passes so our setter can run quicker plays, which can come off as awkward sometimes, but I’m willing to meet halfway. Let’s run your 10-minute routine next practice, I’ll help lead the 3-person continuous drill with you and we can add a short pressure target drill so I can work on adjusting my touch — and yes to simple cues like “mine” and “set.”

transcript.speaker: Samuel Anderson
transcript.content: Thanks, Ethan — I appreciate you being open. Let’s run the 10-minute routine next practice; I’ll bring cones/targets and we can co-lead the 3-person continuous drill. How about we slot the short pressure target drill right after target passing and finish with a 2-minute debrief to lock in cues like “mine” and “set”? Cool if I set that order or would you prefer a different sequence?

transcript.speaker: Ethan Johnson
transcript.content: Sounds perfect — go ahead and set that order. I do want to keep a few reps focused on softer, placement-style passes during target passing so our setter can hit quicker plays, but I'm happy to run the sequence you suggested (target passing → pressure target → 3-person continuous) and co-lead the continuous drill with you. Two-minute debrief to lock in cues works for me.
